subject: dplyr: group_by() should accept a vector of column names

messages.author: 959bc93af75e7478
messages.subject: dplyr: group_by() should accept a vector of column names
parts:
Hi all, 

 unless I missed something, group_by() excepts the user to submit the grouping variables/expressions as arguments. This is very convenient in most case, but quite often, I have to group by columns from a separate list. This leads to awkward syntax like do.call(group_by, c(list(my_df), as.list(column.names))) or forces me to use the grouped_df() function, as in  grouped_df(my_df, as.list(column.names))

 It would be nice if one could have an optional parameter like

   group_by(my_df, group.vars = column.names)

In addition, it would also be useful to have some features of select() in group_by(), e.g.

  group_by(my_df, factor0:factor5)
  group_by(my_df, -x, -y)

Thanks!

-- t.

messages.subject: Re: dplyr: group_by() should accept a vector of column names
parts:
HI TZ,

Although its not as well documented yet, you can use the regroup option to pass a list in a similar fashion to what you are going for.

an example:


groups <- c("vs", "cyl")
grouped <- mtcars %>% regroup(as.list(groups)) 
grouped %>% summarize(mean_mpg = mean(mpg))


Devin

messages.author: f2961c15f7afbca6
messages.subject: Re: dplyr: group_by() should accept a vector of column names
parts:
Oh, and as to merging the select and group functionalities - the slight increase in brevity, IMO, is not nearly worth the reduction in readability and would be a nightmare to distinguish between which columns you were specifying to group vs select. Especially given how easy it is to chain things together.

Alas, if you really want something you could easily roll your own in a simple function along the lines of

select_grouper <- function(df, group_list, ...) {
df %>% regroup(group_list) %>% select(...)
}

select_grouper(mtcars, group_list=list("vs", "cyl"), mpg, disp, hp)

messages.subject: Re: dplyr: group_by() should accept a vector of column names
parts:
Hi Devin, 

 thank you for the hint on regroup(), this is very useful!

 As to the second part of my post, I haven't probably explained very well what I meant. I completely agree that merging select and group_by would be a horrible idea. What I meant is that select allows for some very neat syntactic sugar, like

  select(-x) # select everything but x
  select(x0:x5) # select all columns between x0 and x5

in the data I work with (linguistics), it is often the case that most columns define groups. Therefore, having similar syntax for group would be very nice:


  group_by(-x) # group by all columns but x
  group_by(x0:x5) # group by the columns between x0 and x5

I guess this can be implemented by mixing the functionality of  select_vars into group_by...

Best, 

 t.
